summary: Round 3's fixes are in place: seven of its eight findings are closed at the lines cited, and R3-5 still holds and is carried. All 11 coverage candidates were verified, and most sit where #93's new decisions meet older code. NOT_YOURS now reaches the plan approver and the resolve agent, whose jobs reopen a shaper's decision. An unresolved override, a stale deferred entry and a renamed id fall through bookkeeping written before declines existed. The human-review path still reads newHead where the main loop now reads what was fixed. The Docs and Version steps hold (0.3.0 against main's 0.2.4, a Docs entry for every touched plugin file), and the repository has no scheduled or queued work.

findings.title: The human-review finding template still writes needsDecision, which #93 removed from the finding contract
findings.description: The finding template this skill builds for each teammate comment still carries `"needsDecision": false` (line 19). This pull request removed the field from FINDING_SCHEMA, the reviewer, the shaper and `skills/redline/SKILL.md`. R1-4 fixed it in that file only (6a8c63a); this file is not in that fix or in this pull request's diff. Human findings never pass through review(), so the `delete f.needsDecision` at workflows/redline-loop.js:2321 never runs on them. The field reaches humanShapePrompt's findings JSON (workflows/redline-loop.js:1682), and no instruction defines it. The loop test's human fixtures carry it too (tests/loop-test.mjs:904, 1149, 2096, 2249, 2372). It is always false, so nothing behaves differently today. Two readings: it is a leftover to remove, or it stays on purpose. The pull request says a human review pass's own prompts are as they were, and removing the field changes the bytes of that pass's shaper prompt.
findings.proposedFix: Drop `"needsDecision": false` from the template at line 19 and from the loop test's human fixtures. Or record in the #93 spec's shape.md that the human pass keeps it so its prompts stay unchanged.

findings.title: rulesBlock still says a rule-covered finding is never fixed or deferred, and leaves decline out
findings.description:
The ask-rules text goes into the shaper's, the reshape's and the plan approver's prompts (rulesBlock, line 446). It says a covered finding is 'never fixed or deferred by Redline', and that the approver bounces 'a task that writes under a paths rule or fixes a finding a prose rule covers'. This pull request made decline a disposition and updated the same rule elsewhere: the shaper's rule 7 says 'never fix, decline or defer' (agents/redline-shaper.md:29), the skill says 'never fixed, declined or deferred by Redline' (skills/redline/SKILL.md:98), and forceAskRules's comment names decline (line 2698). Line 446 is unchanged by the diff.

The prompt's positive sentence ('in the shaper's JSON it is ask') still directs an ask, so the omission alone does not license a decline. Little stands behind that sentence for a prose rule. forceAskRules forces a prose rule only from the shaper's own askRule tag (lines 2719-2720); it does not read the reviewer's tag. A decline has no task, so neither rulesBlock's approver sentence nor the approver's point 5 ('a fix or defer task', agents/redline-plan-approver.md:20) can bounce it. Before this pull request, every non-ask disposition had a task the approver could bounce.

So a shaper that declines a prose-covered finding without tagging it is posted 'declined:' and its thread is resolved at Finish. The inline comment meanwhile says the finding is left to the person (commentBody, line 1126, reads the reviewer's tag through ruleOf). Conditions: a repository with a prose ask rule, and a shaper that declines a covered finding against its prompt and its agent file.
findings.proposedFix: Say 'never fixed, declined or deferred by Redline' in rulesBlock. Add that a decline of a finding a prose rule covers is a bounce, in rulesBlock's approver sentence and in point 5 of agents/redline-plan-approver.md. Optionally have forceAskRules also read the reviewer's askRule tag (ruleOf) for prose rules. The prompts change only in repositories that declare ask rules.

findings.title: With no login, decisionSentence's fallback starts a sentence in lowercase
findings.description: This pull request changed decisionSentence's fallback for a Redline round from 'The author chose: ...' to `${personLabel} chose: ...` (line 1135). With no login, personLabel is 'the person running Redline'. In a human-review run's final nit pass, which is a Redline round, it is 'the author' (line 190). The reply then reads 'Redline round 2: the person running Redline chose: Keep it. No code change. · decided by: the person running Redline' (replyBody, line 1295), and the handoff line carries the same sentence (describeOutcome, line 2567). R1-17 fixed the same lowercase start in capComment only (line 3388), so this is a second site with the same cause, not a reopening of that fix. Conditions: args.login is empty and a decision has empty notes. The skill always passes a login from `redline-gh.sh login` and always writes notes, and autopilot decisions carry notes, so only a hand-built relaunch reaches it.
findings.proposedFix: Capitalise the label where it starts the sentence, as capComment does since R1-17: `${human ? 'The author' : personLabel.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + personLabel.slice(1)} chose: ${decision.choice}.` Add a loop check for no login and a decision with no notes.

findings.title: The resolve prompt says to apply an overruled decline, then that a shaper's decline is never reopened
findings.description:
For a Redline round, resolvePrompt lists the person's disposition overrides and says 'a finding the shaper declined is overruled the same way' (line 1742). It then closes with decideRule(pass), which for a Redline round is NOT_YOURS (lines 343, 354, 1748): 'A decision already made, the shaper's own included (a fix, a decline with its reason, a deferral), is applied as recorded and never reopened.' Overruling a decline is exactly reopening the shaper's decline, so one prompt says both. Before this pull request the line carried NEVER_DECIDE, which has no 'never reopened' clause. The agent file says the overrule is applied (agents/redline-resolve.md:14, 21); the prompt's last rule says the opposite.

A resolve agent that follows the last rule does one of two things. It keeps the decline, which is posted 'declined:' and its thread resolved at Finish, against the person's line. Or it lists the finding under unresolved, which on guided gives a stop with no question on it (R4-8).

The implementer and the plan approver are shown the effective disposition (lines 2958-2961, 2970, 3053), so the overruled decline reaches them as fix and the clash is weaker there. The loop test scripts the resolve agent, so whether a real one keeps the decline is not measured; the contradiction is in the prompt text.
findings.proposedFix: In resolvePrompt's Redline branch, replace NOT_YOURS with the rule the resolve agent needs: a pending decision is the person's; a disposition override is the person's decision and replaces the shaper's, a decline included; every other decision is applied as recorded. Pin the sentence in the loop test beside the existing 'Disposition overrides' check (tests/loop-test.mjs:2297).

findings.title: The plan approver is told the shaper's fix, decline and deferral are never reopened, though its bounces reopen them
findings.proposedFix: Give the approver's Redline branch its own sentence in place of NOT_YOURS: a pending decision is the person's and the approver never decides it; the person's decisions (the roundDecisions block) are applied as recorded; the shaper's own dispositions are what the approver checks, as its instructions say. In reshapePrompt's Redline branch, say that a decided entry an adjustment names is decided again. Pin both in the loop test.

findings.title: A renamed reviewer id can collide with an id another finding already has
findings.proposedFix: Number a renamed id after the highest id in use, as reconcilePrior does: compute `next` from the ids that already match, then give each one that does not match `R<round>-<++next>`, keeping the rename map. Add a loop check with ids ['R2-1', 'R2-3', 'X'] and a coverage ref to R2-3.

findings.title: checkWhy runs after the spec-status agent call, so a refused reason first costs that call
findings.description: At this head, revise() still runs checkSpec, which starts the `spec status` GitHub agent (line 2671), before forceAskRules and checkWhy: lines 2876-2878 after the shape, and 2994-2996 after a reshape. forceAskRules reads only record, pass, inScope and shaped, so it and checkWhy could run first. In this order, a why_human that checkWhy refuses costs one agent call before the stop. checkWhy also has to be passed the shaper's label explicitly, since lastLabel names the spec check (R2-9, line 2651). The shaper's schema already refuses a reason outside ROUND_WHY and the rule reasons (judgmentCallSchema, line 651, used by SHAPE_SCHEMAS at line 722), so the throw is reached only when that structured output is not enforced. Round 3's shape.md records a decline of this finding in its Declined section: the spec check's diagnosis of a halted shaper (#57) runs first and is worth the one call. No reply reached the thread, so the finding is carried. It is a cost and an ordering point, not wrong behaviour.
findings.proposedFix: Run forceAskRules and checkWhy before checkSpec at both sites, keep the explicit shaper label, and check that the loop test's replay prefixes still hold. Or post round 3's recorded decline as this finding's decision.

findings.title: A disposition override the resolve agent cannot apply stops the run with no question to answer
findings.description:
When the resolve agent returns an id under unresolved, resolveWith hands back `pending: newCalls.filter((call) => ids.includes(call.id))` (line 2945). An override is not a call, so an unresolved override is left out of pending. handoffResult then returns judgmentCalls [] and decisionsNeeded [] (lines 3648, 3682). It also leaves the overruled decline out of `declined`, since its decision carries a disposition (line 3664). The id appears only in `unresolved` (line 3681), which the skill never reads (nothing in skills/ or docs/ mentions it).

Trace on guided:
1. At the first stop the person types `R1-7: defer. keep it small`.
2. On relaunch, overridesFor picks it up (line 2916).
3. The first resolve finds the mitigation too unclear and leaves it pending, as agents/redline-resolve.md:29 tells it to.
4. The stop has nothing to present, so every call in decisionsNeeded counts as answered, and the skill asks for `relaunch` (skills/redline/SKILL.md:214).
5. The relaunch has the same args, so the resolve prompt is identical and replays its cached unresolved result. The run stops at the same empty hand-off every time.

The filter predates this pull request (main line 2758), and a plan-dial override could already reach it. This pull request changed the line (adding shaped and afterApproval) and adds a new way in: the typed decline overrule at a decisions stop. On autopilot the same path is a stageError that names 'the shaper's recommendation' (line 2943).
findings.proposedFix: Carry an unresolved override into the hand-off: list it in the stop's result, for example under `declined` with the resolve agent's why, or as an entry the skill must ask again. Have the skill present `unresolved` and ask the person to restate the line before `relaunch`. Loop check: a guided stop with a typed defer overrule that the resolve returns unresolved names that id in the hand-off.

findings.title: A deferred entry beside a decline is listed under Deferred as shipped
findings.description:
Every entry in the round's `deferred` list goes into deferredAll, whatever its finding's final disposition (lines 3109-3112). outcomesFor files a finding as deferred only when its disposition is defer (line 2541). So a declined finding with a deferred entry is posted 'declined: <reason>', and the handoff also lists it under '### Deferred (mitigated now, full fix left open)' as 'shipped <mitigation>' (lines 3283-3285). The skill's `done` walk then offers it as a deferral whose mitigation shipped (skills/redline/SKILL.md:240).

The entry gets there two ways:
- The shaper returns a decline with a stray deferred entry. Nothing checks deferred ids against defer dispositions (checkDispositions, lines 2585-2620).
- A reshape re-sorts a defer to a decline. Line 3004 keeps every earlier deferred entry the reshape's list does not name, so the first shaper's entry survives.

The implementer's and the approver's prompts also get the stale entry beside the decline (lines 1771, 1849). Both lines predate this pull request (main lines 2816 and 2921), where a defer re-sorted to fix showed the same double listing. This pull request adds decline, a disposition with no task and no commit, so the Deferred line now claims a mitigation that never shipped.
findings.proposedFix: Push to deferredAll only the items outcomesFor files as deferred: move the loop after outcomesFor and filter on `outcomes[item.id].kind === 'deferred'`. At line 3004, drop an earlier entry whose finding the reshape sorted to something other than defer. A warning in checkDispositions for a deferred id whose disposition is not defer would show the stray case. Loop check: a reshape that re-sorts R1-4 from defer to decline leaves it out of Deferred.

findings.title: A correctness fix the person changes to accept on the plan dial still buys a round
findings.description:
`bought` reads the shaper's own disposition before any override (shaperOwn, lines 3131 and 3165). So a correctness item the shaper sorted as fix, which the person changed to accept on the plan dial, still buys the next round: a coverage pass and a verify at an unchanged head (range.empty, line 3920), and one more round toward the cap. A decline the person overrules to fix also buys, through finalOwn, so the two overrides act differently.

Two readings. In the first, the code is as intended. It follows decision 1 of the #93 spec ('a new correctness item that the shaper fixes or puts to the person ... whatever the person answered', agent-os/specs/2026-11-13-1139-93-verify-facts-shaper-decides/shape.md:42) and docs/running.md:43 ('This holds whatever you answered ... after a round you answered with "no change"'). The comment at lines 3127-3130 says the shaper's disposition is read on purpose: the finder was still producing correctness material. In the second, a plan-dial accept takes the item off the table: nothing was fixed or put to the person as a call, and the extra round is only a cost.

No loop check covers a plan-dial accept of a fix (tests/loop-test.mjs, section 19). It is a cost, not wrong output.
findings.proposedFix: Keep it, and say so in docs/running.md:43 (a fix you change to accept on the plan dial still buys the round). Or exclude it: in the shaperOwn branch, skip an item whose finalOwn is accept. Either way, add a loop check for a plan-dial accept of a correctness fix.

findings.title: The handoff's overrule line names the runner's login, so a teammate's reply is not read
findings.description: The Declined by Redline heading tells the reader to reply in the thread, then run `/redline:redline-revise <pr> review @<login>` filled with the login of the person running Redline (line 3275). The handoff is addressed to the teammate ('`@<teammate>`, over to you', line 3220). The `@login` selector keeps only comments by that login (scripts/redline-gh.sh:428-432). A teammate who replies in a declined thread, and then runs the posted command or has the runner run it, gets a pass that does not see their reply. When the reply is the only open comment, the pass stops with 'nothing to revise for that selector' (skills/redline-revise/SKILL.md:16). docs/running.md:114 says 'A teammate overrules the same way from their own review', meaning with their own login, but the posted line never says so. The PR description states the after-run door as `review @<login>` without saying whose login.
findings.proposedFix: Say whose login goes in the command, e.g. 'then run `/redline:redline-revise <pr> review @<the login that replied>`' (with `review @<runner>` for a reply of the runner's own). Update the loop checks that pin the line, and docs/running.md:114.

findings.title: A human review pass that fixed nothing still runs and posts a final nit pass over an empty diff
findings.description:
The human-review path runs its final nit pass when `outcome.newHead` is set (line 3726). newHead is the last of the round's new commits (line 3152). The implementer always commits the spec folder as task 1 (agents/redline-implementer.md:17), so newHead is set even when every comment was `none` or an ask answered with no change.

The nit pass then reviews `git diff <startSha>..<newHead> -- ':/' ':(top,exclude)agent-os/specs'` (line 1333), which is empty when the only commit is the spec folder. It posts a 'Redline round N' review for that diff (line 3745), which uses up a round number later runs would have used. The summary says 'Final nit pass (Redline round N): no correctness bugs.' (line 3373), where humanSummary's own sentence for this case is 'No commits, so no final nit pass.' (line 3371).

In this pull request the main loop moved to the commits that fixed something (`fixed`, lines 3166 and 3910; R1-20), but this site still reads newHead. The line is unchanged from main (line 3429).
findings.proposedFix: Gate the human path's nit pass on `outcome.fixed.length > 0`, as the main loop gates on fixedAny, and keep newHead as the range's end. Reword the no-pass sentence to 'No fix was committed, so no final nit pass.' Loop check: a human pass whose only finding is `none` posts no Redline round and gets that sentence.

list.summary: planPrompt gives a Redline round's plan approver NOT_YOURS, which says the shaper's own fix, decline or deferral is applied as recorded and never reopened. That contradicts the approver's agent-file duties to bounce some declines (an unconfirmed finding that is serious if true, or a reason no one can check) and some fixes (disproportionate, or a refactor failing the four tests). The reshape prompt (line 1708) adds that decided Decisions entries stay as they are.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper declines an unconfirmed finding whose harm would be serious if true (say a possible double charge), reason 'could not confirm: needs two workers'. The plan approver is the only layer that enforces 'never a decline on Redline's own say'. Its prompt says the shaper's decline is never reopened, so it approves, and the decline is posted and its thread resolved at Finish. If it does bounce, the reshape is told decided entries stay as they are, so it keeps the decline. The approver bounces again, and after maxPlanAdjustments the run stops at stage 'approve'. The same applies to a disproportionate `fix`, which the approver could bounce before this PR.

list.summary: When the resolve agent cannot apply a disposition override, the hand-off's pending list keeps only judgment calls, so it carries no question at all. #93 adds a new way in: a typed decline overrule at a decisions stop.
list.failure_scenario: At a guided stop the person types 'R1-7: defer. keep it small'. On relaunch the first resolve finds the mitigation too vague and returns unresolved [{id:'R1-7'}]. resolveWith returns pending = newCalls.filter(ids.includes) = [], so handoffResult gives judgmentCalls [] and decisionsNeeded [], with unresolved [R1-7]. The skill never reads `unresolved`. Since every call in decisionsNeeded counts as answered, it asks for `relaunch` straight away. The relaunch has the same args, so the cached resolve replays the same unresolved result and the run stops at the same empty hand-off every time. Plan-dial overrides hit the same path.

list.summary: resolvePrompt tells the resolve agent to apply a person's overrule of a shaper decline (line 1742), then ends with decideRule(pass), which is NOT_YOURS: 'A decision already made, the shaper's own included (... a decline with its reason ...), is applied as recorded and never reopened.' The same conflict reaches the implementer through implementPrompt.
list.failure_scenario: The person overrules decline R1-7 to fix. The resolve prompt says to plan the fix and, a few lines later, that the shaper's decline is never reopened. A resolve agent that follows the final rule keeps the decline and lists R1-7 under unresolved. That then triggers the empty hand-off loop above, or on autopilot a stageError('resolve').

list.summary: The handoff's overrule instruction always names the runner's login (`review @<login>`). The human-review selector keeps only comments by that login, so a teammate who replies in a declined thread is not picked up when that command is run.
list.failure_scenario: The handoff ends '@sam, over to you'. Sam replies 'please fix this' in R1-3's thread. The runner then runs `/redline:redline-revise 94 review @runner`, as the line says. `human-review @runner` drops comments by other logins, so Sam's overrule is never ingested. docs/running.md says a teammate overrules 'from their own review', which would need `review @sam`; the posted line never says so.

list.summary: `bought` reads the shaper's own disposition, so a correctness `fix` that the person changed to `accept` on the plan dial still buys another full round. A decline overruled to fix does change what is bought, so the two overrides are treated differently.
list.failure_scenario: Plan dial: the shaper sorts correctness R2-1 as fix. The person changes it to 'accept. The behaviour is intended.' Nothing is fixed or put to them, but shaperOwn['R2-1'] === 'fix' makes bought true. With coverage on, the run starts round 3: a full code-review coverage pass and a verify over an unchanged head (range.empty). That spends a round and can move the run toward the cap. docs/running.md:43 says a round is bought by a correctness item the shaper fixed or put to the person.

list.summary: The human-review path still decides whether to run its final nit pass from `outcome.newHead`. The implementer's spec-folder commit always sets it, whereas the main loop now uses the commits that fixed something (`fixed`; #93, R1-20).
list.failure_scenario: In a human review pass every comment is `none` or an ask answered 'no change'. The only new commit is 'redline: save review round ... spec', so newHead is set. The pass then gathers, runs a final nit pass over a diff that excludes agent-os/specs (so it is empty), and posts a 'Redline round N' review for it, using up a round number. The summary says 'Final nit pass (Redline round N): no correctness bugs.' even though no code changed.

list.summary: Every entry in the shaper's `deferred` list goes into deferredAll whatever that finding's disposition. A `decline` with a stray deferred entry is therefore posted as declined and also listed under Deferred as shipped.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper declines R1-4 and also returns deferred [{id:'R1-4', mitigation:'none', fullFix:'follow-up issue'}]. outcomesFor files it as 'declined' (the defer branch needs disposition 'defer'). The handoff then lists R1-4 under 'Declined by Redline' and under '### Deferred (mitigated now, full fix left open)' as 'shipped none', and the skill's deferred walk offers to open an issue for a mitigation that never shipped. Nothing checks deferred ids against defer dispositions.

list.summary: rulesBlock, the ask-rules text in the shaper, reshape and plan approver prompts, still says a covered finding is 'never fixed or deferred by Redline' and leaves out decline. The shaper agent file says 'never fix, decline or defer'.
list.failure_scenario: A prose ask rule covers R1-2. The shaper, following its prompt, declines it without setting askRule. forceAskRules forces a prose rule only from the shaper's own askRule tag, so the decline stands. A finding the repository reserves for the person is turned down by Redline, posted 'declined:', and its thread resolved.

list.summary: An invalid reviewer id is renamed to R<round>-<index+1> without checking whether another finding already has that id. The new accountCoverage byId map and the minted ids then work from a duplicated id.
list.failure_scenario: The reviewer returns ids ['R2-1', 'R2-3', 'X'] (it skipped a number). 'X' becomes R2-3, a duplicate. byId keeps the last R2-3, so a coverage ref 'R2-3' is counted against the wrong finding. post's commentIds map holds one comment id for both, replies and the thread sweep go to one thread, and prior-findings later reads two lines with the same id.

list.summary: decisionSentence's fallback for a Redline round starts a sentence with personLabel, which is lowercase with no login ('the person running Redline', or 'the author' in a human run's final nit pass). R1-17 fixed the same thing only in capComment.
list.failure_scenario: No login, and a decision with empty notes. The reply reads 'Redline round 2: the person running Redline chose: Keep it. No code change. · decided by: the person running Redline', and the handoff line carries the same lowercase sentence.

list.summary: The human-review finding template still writes `"needsDecision": false`, a field #93 removed from the finding contract everywhere else (schema, skill, reviewer, shaper).
list.failure_scenario: Each human-review pass passes needsDecision into the shaper's findings JSON, but no instruction defines it any more. That leaves a dead field the shaper may read as a decision flag, and it disagrees with the rest of the #93 contract (agent-os/standards/workflow/agents.md: a changed rule is applied everywhere it is stated).
